## Get a webhook when an eval task fails

October 29, 2026New Webhooks and EventsSubscribe a webhook to the new`ONLINE_TASK_RUN_FAILED` event, so you hear when an eval task stops writing evals, such as after an API key expires or a model is retired, instead of finding gaps in your metrics days later. Attach a webhook to one task from the **Webhooks**button in its logs, or to every task in a space, including tasks created later, from the REST API, the Python SDK, or the

`ax` CLI.
- **When it fires**: A run fails, scores some evals and then stops on an error (payload `status` is `partial_completed`), or cannot start because the task’s config is invalid. Runs a user stops and runs with no data stay quiet.
- **One alert per cause**: A task that fails the same way on every run alerts once. It alerts again when the `error_type` changes, or on the next failure after a run completes.
- **Payload**: The task, run, and project or dataset IDs, an `error_type` such as `rate_limit`, `authentication`, or `run_timeout`, the failure text, and a link to the run’s logs.
- **Config errors in run logs**: When a scheduled run fails on an invalid config, the task’s run logs now show a `failed` run with the reason.
- **Stopped runs**: A run you stop now always ends `cancelled` and keeps the counts it scored.
- **Versions**: Python `arize` 8.61.0 or later for `ONLINE_TASK` and `SPACE` sources.

For more information, refer to the webhooks documentation.

## Run managed agents on the OpenCode harness

October 23, 2026New AgentsOpenCode joins Claude Code, Codex, and Cursor as a harness for managed agents, and it is now available on every account. Choose it per run in Agent Studio, save it on an agent config, or select it when configuring Signal. OpenCode runs on Claude Sonnet 4.6 and uses your own Anthropic AI provider.For more information, refer to the Connect your harness documentation.
## Fixes and improvements

October 26–28, 2026
**SDKs and REST APIs**

- Improvement Adopt the experiments SDK methods without pre-release warnings; experiments are now marked stable in the Python, JavaScript, and Go clients.
- Fix Send traces through an authenticated HTTP or HTTPS proxy from the Python SDK, which now passes the proxy URL credentials as a `Proxy-Authorization` header.

**Models and Integrations**

- Fix Point the Vertex AI Gemini integration at a gateway that routes only the stable `/v1` API by ending the base URL in `/v1`; a base URL ending in `/v1` or `/v1beta1` is now used as-is.

**Dashboards and Visualizations**

- Fix Apply a model-scoped filter on a multi-model dashboard without blanking widgets for the other models; each dashboard filter now applies only to its own model.

**Custom Metrics**

- Fix Compute custom metrics across the full time range you are viewing; schema discovery now covers that range so the metric’s columns resolve.

**Annotations**

- Fix See an annotation queue record marked complete as soon as your submission saves, matching the status the server records.

**Alyx**

- Improvement Ask Alyx to create and run Decision Judge evaluators on your Perplexity or Cloudflare integration, either by naming the provider or by letting Alyx select it.
- Fix Move past an Alyx proposal by sending a new message; the proposal is marked superseded instead of staying pending indefinitely.

## Find and fix eval gaps with the Eval Health agent

October 21, 2026New EvaluatorsEval Health is a managed agent that reviews the evals on a tracing project and proposes changes for you to accept. It reads the project’s recent spans, tasks, and evaluators, then files an issue for each coverage gap or broken eval it finds, along with a proposed action:
- **Create:** add an eval for a part of your app that isn’t covered yet.
- **Fix:** repair an eval in place, such as its column mappings, query filter, or template and labels.
- **Delete:** remove an eval that’s no longer producing useful signal.
- **Optimize:** cut eval cost by converting an LLM judge to a code eval or suggesting a different judge model.

Nothing changes until you accept it. Every proposal is ready to run the moment you approve it, and a run that finds sufficient coverage proposes nothing. Find it by adding the Eval Health Agent on any tracing project.

## Score whole conversations with trace and session remote evaluators

October 21, 2026Improvement EvaluatorsAt trace and session scope, a remote evaluator now receives each mapped variable as an array with one value per span instead of a single comma-joined string, so your endpoint can score an entire conversation in one call. Spans are ordered by start time, each trace’s spans stay together, and every variable’s array covers the same spans in the same order, so index`i` refers to the same span across all variables. This is the default for every trace and session remote evaluator; span scope is unchanged.
- Spans with no value appear as `null`, so each variable’s array stays aligned with the others.
- Variables that exceed the size cap are truncated, and `metadata.truncated_variables` lists which ones were cut.

## Run trace and session evaluators on datasets

October 20, 2026New Datasets and ExperimentsTrace-level and session-level evaluators can now run over a dataset, not only over live projects and experiments, so you can score multi-span traces and full sessions from data you have already collected. The evaluator groups the dataset’s rows into trace or session units and writes one verdict per unit instead of scoring each row on its own. If you created such a task through the API or SDK, it switches from per-row to per-unit scoring.Learn more about trace and session evaluations.
## Run Decision Judge evaluations on Perplexity and Cloudflare decision models

October 20, 2026New EvaluatorsPerplexity and Cloudflare are now available as Decision Judge providers in Arize AX, so you can run Decision Judge evaluations with your own key on Perplexity’s`pplx-decider-v1.1-27b` or Cloudflare’s Clef models (`clef` and `clef-flash`). These integrations are used only by Decision Judge evaluators and do not appear in the Playground or LLM-as-a-Judge.Learn more about Decision Judge.
## Track Claude Code spend by model and user

October 20, 2026New Models and IntegrationsA new Anthropic Console cost connector pulls Claude Code usage and spend from Anthropic’s Claude Code Analytics API, so you can track what your organization spends on Claude Code and break it down by model and by user. Connect it with an Anthropic Admin key to import daily token usage and estimated cost.Learn more about tracking costs.
## Restrict Alyx to one AI provider and model

October 20, 2026New AlyxSpace admins can now lock Alyx to a single AI provider and model from Space Settings, so everyone in the space works through an approved model and Alyx rejects requests for any other one. Once a model is set, members see it fixed in the Alyx model picker.Learn more about Alyx.
## Edit a saved dashboard’s scope and name

October 20, 2026Improvement Dashboards and VisualizationsYou can now rename an account dashboard and change its saved scope after creating it, using the Edit button on the dashboard. Point it at the entire account, specific organizations, or specific spaces without rebuilding the dashboard, and its default time range is preserved.Learn more about dashboards.
## Fixes and improvements

October 20–21, 2026
**Evaluators**

- Improvement See how many rows an evaluation skipped and why: run summaries now count rows skipped for null input values and name the columns responsible, so successes, skips, and failures account for every row fetched.

**Datasets and Experiments**

- Fix Stop a task run and get an accurate status: the run is marked cancelled, keeps the counts it scored before stopping, and a fully-skipped run reports the reason.

**Playground**

- Fix Saving a prompt version to the hub now persists the full set of model parameters, including unchanged defaults, so a reloaded prompt reproduces the original configuration.
- Fix Open prompts saved from spans that contain tool calls in the prompt playground.

**Tracing and Sessions**

- Fix Build trace filters that hold: NULL checks commit as is empty or exists, OR connectors stay OR after you clear a row, pasted SQL filters parse correctly, and View Traces from the agent graph keeps your filter.

**Annotations**

- Fix View a session’s traces and compare them from an annotation queue: View All Traces uses the session’s own time window, and trace comparison works on queue routes.

**Custom Metrics**

- Fix Trigger a managed agent on any custom metric in its space, not only a metric defined in the trigger’s own project.

**Agents**

- Improvement Disconnect a connected Slack workspace from your account on the Slack Agents settings page, rather than only removing individual channel bindings.

**Alyx**

- Fix Accept an Alyx custom metric proposal on production-only and multi-environment models: Alyx now validates a proposed metric against the environment the target model actually uses.
- Improvement Attach up to 16 custom request-metadata pairs to Alyx calls on an AWS Bedrock integration, so your own Bedrock logs attribute usage to Arize AX users.

**Models and Integrations**

- Improvement Track OpenAI spend using the per-API-key costs reported by OpenAI’s Costs API, so per-key and per-project totals match your actual bill.

## Build and run Decision Judge evaluators with Alyx

October 19, 2026New AlyxYou can now ask Alyx to create, edit, and run Decision Judge evaluators from chat, so you can go from a description of what to check to scored spans. Alyx fills in the state template and typed questions in the Decision Judge editor, and nothing saves until you accept it. It works with any Decision Judge provider in your space, including Jev-as-a-Judge on TypeSafe AI; name one, such as OpenAI, to use it.
- **Run**: Alyx reuses a matching evaluator or proposes a new one, creates a project task, checks its column mappings, and runs it over historical LLM spans.
- **Edit**: Accepted changes to the state template, questions, or description save as a new version.
- **Explain**: Alyx shows an evaluator’s model, integration, state template, and the criteria for each question.

Learn more about Decision Judge.

## Run Decision Judge evals on OpenAI decision models

October 16, 2026Improvement EvaluatorsJev-as-a-Judge is now
**Decision Judge**, a provider-neutral evaluator type. The same shared state and typed boolean, choice, and score questions can run on TypeSafe AI’s

`jev-latest` or OpenAI’s `gpt-6-luna` through your existing OpenAI integration. Pick the provider from the AI Provider dropdown in the evaluator editor; only integrations in your space that can run Decision Judge evaluations are listed. Most Arize eval templates now have a Decision Judge version, loaded by selecting a TypeSafe AI model on the template card.Existing Jev-as-a-Judge evaluators keep working unchanged. Links to the old docs page redirect to the new one.Learn more about Decision Judge.
## Reference a range monitor’s second threshold in alert notes

October 13, 2026Improvement Webhooks and EventsWhen you compose a monitor’s alert note, you can now insert the second threshold of a range monitor with the`{{threshold2.operator}}` and `{{threshold2.value}}` variables, so an alert can state both bounds of the range that triggered it. For example, a note of `Metric is {{threshold2.operator}} {{threshold2.value}}` renders the evaluated second bound in each alert. The two variables appear in the variable picker on the **Monitor Notes**field, in the

**Notifications**section of the monitor configuration, and only when the monitor’s threshold mode is set to range. The existing

`{{threshold.operator}}` and `{{threshold.value}}` variables continue to reference the first threshold.For more information, refer to the monitor notifications documentation.
## Filter traces by clicking a bar on an eval chart

October 12, 2026Improvement Tracing and SessionsOn the
**Evals and Metrics**tab in LLM tracing, you can now click a bar on an eval chart card to filter the traces by that eval label. The full column is clickable, so you can also filter by short bars and labels such as N/A that were previously hard to target. The same action is available as a

**Filter by label**submenu in each card’s overflow menu.Learn more about viewing and managing traces.

## Turn a Signal issue into a running evaluator from the issue

October 9, 2026Improvement AlyxClick
**Create Evaluator**on a Signal issue, and Alyx builds an evaluator for that failure pattern and starts scoring new traces with it. Alyx creates a continuous task with no historical backfill and sets up its filters and column mappings automatically. If the chat is closed, Alyx works in the background; when it finishes,

**View Task**in the notification opens the task on the current page.

## Fixes and improvements

October 8–14, 2026
- Fix  Tracing and Sessions Keep building span filters without losing your in-progress text: **Add Filter** in the trace filter bar now appends the next filter instead of replacing the one you are editing.
- Fix  Tracing and Sessions Display and filter tracing columns whose names contain dots, such as a `workflow.name` metadata key, a dotted prompt-template variable, or an annotation like `quality.v2`.
- Fix SDKs and REST APIs Call the Python SDK against a server of a different version without errors when a REST response omits fields the client expects.
- Fix  CLI Commands Run `ax ai-integrations list` to list a space’s AI integrations even when the space contains a TypeSafe AI integration.

## Create and manage webhooks from the REST API, SDKs, and CLI

October 7, 2026New Webhooks and EventsYou can now create webhooks and subscribe them to prompt and evaluator events from the REST API, the Python, TypeScript, and Go SDKs, or the`ax` CLI, so you can script event delivery to your own systems, such as a CI job that runs when a prompt version gets a new label. A webhook is an HTTPS endpoint in your organization that authenticates each delivery with a bearer token or an HMAC-SHA256 signature. A subscription connects one webhook to one event on one prompt or evaluator. These endpoints are in alpha and may change without notice.
- **Events**: `PROMPT_VERSION_CREATED`, `PROMPT_VERSION_LABELED`, and `PROMPT_VERSION_UNLABELED` for prompts; `EVALUATOR_VERSION_CREATED` for evaluators.
- **Tests and delivery history**: Send a test delivery to a bearer-token webhook, and list each webhook’s delivery attempts, including retries.
- **Signing secrets**: Arize AX returns an HMAC-SHA256 webhook’s signing secret only once, in the create response, so store it when you create the webhook.
- **Versions**: Python `arize` 8.54.0 or later (`client.webhooks`), TypeScript `@arizeai/ax-client` 1.30.0 or later, Go SDK v2 v0.24.0 or later, and `arize-ax-cli` 0.39.0 or later (`ax webhooks`).

## Filter spans by nested JSON attributes with path typeahead

October 6, 2026New Tracing and SessionsWhen you build a span filter on the tracing page, Arize AX now suggests nested JSON attribute paths as you type, so you can drill into structured span attributes without recalling the exact path. Clicking a nested attribute value in a span adds it to your filter directly. The feature is available on every account tier across cloud and self-hosted deployments.For more information, refer to the view and manage traces documentation.

## Select GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Sonnet 5.5 in the Playground

October 1, 2026New Models and IntegrationsTwo new models are available for prompts and evaluations in Arize AX: OpenAI’s GPT-6.1 Sol and Anthropic’s Claude Sonnet 5.5. Select either from the model picker in the Playground to run prompts, build evaluators, or power online tasks.
- **GPT-6.1 Sol**: available on OpenAI and Azure OpenAI, with a 128,000-token completion limit and configurable reasoning effort.
- **Claude Sonnet 5.5**: available on Anthropic, AWS Bedrock, and Google Vertex AI, with a 128,000-token completion limit and adaptive reasoning effort.

Learn more about supported model providers.

September 29 – October 6, 2026

- Fix View harness projects, such as `claude-code`, on the Tracing Projects page and through the `GET /v2/projects` REST endpoint again; each is marked with a Harness label so it is not mistaken for a production project.
- Fix See a consistent score on task-less evaluator cards in the Tracing project Metrics tab, whether the card is pinned or unpinned.

- Fix See the true dataset row count when Alyx previews a dataset, so it recognizes when a preview covers only part of the data and filters server-side.

## Break down LLM spend on every project with the Cost tab

September 29, 2026New Dashboards and VisualizationsThe Cost tab is now available on every project overview. It surfaces the built-in Cost agent’s analysis of your LLM spend: charts of spend over time and by model, and cost-savings issues that flag expensive models doing low-complexity work with quantified recommendations for cheaper routing. Projects that have not run the Cost agent yet show a preview of what it will surface.Learn more about the Cost agent.
## Build and edit dashboards with Alyx

September 29, 2026New Alyx Dashboards
- **Build a dashboard:** Alyx can create a dashboard from a template or from scratch, then create and edit its time series, distribution, statistic, pivot table, and text widgets. Split a time series into one line per value, such as latency per model.
- **Redesign your dashboards:** Retheme a dashboard, rename several charts, or add new widgets in one request. Alyx can also move, resize, and delete widgets you name.
- **Understand a dashboard:** Ask Alyx to summarize what a dashboard or widget shows. Dashboard and Widget context pills attach what you are looking at to your message.

Learn more about Alyx dashboard capabilities and setting up dashboards.

## Add entire sessions to a dataset from the Sessions view

September 29, 2026New Datasets and ExperimentsYou can now select whole sessions on the Sessions page and add them to a dataset in one step, rather than collecting spans one at a time. Use the checkbox column to pick sessions (or select all), then choose “Add to Dataset” from the selection toolbar; each session is copied into the dataset as examples. The same toolbar can send the selected sessions to a labeling queue.Learn more about curating a dataset.
## Inspect traces and spans inline in the session conversation view

September 29, 2026Improvement Tracing and SessionsThe session conversation tab now lets you drill from a conversation into its underlying telemetry without leaving the session. Select a turn to open its trace tree, then select a span to open span details, all in the same view. A new Session Overview panel summarizes each turn’s latency, token usage, and errors, and shows a pass/fail grid of evaluation results where selecting a result opens the turn it applies to.Learn more about sessions.

September 29, 2026New CLI CommandsThe`ax integrations create llm` command now supports three more providers: LiteLLM, Fireworks, and Together AI. ## Fixes and improvements

September 28–29, 2026
**Datasets and Experiments**

- Fix Page through experiments that have repeated runs and receive complete, per-run results, with a separate evaluation result recorded for each repeated run.
- Fix Attach custom code evaluators that use the reserved `dataset_row` parameter to an online task without mapping it to a data column.
- Fix Run an evaluator on an experiment after running it on the parent dataset, so the experiment evaluation completes.

**Webhooks and Events**

## Run high-volume structured evals with Jev-as-a-Judge

September 26, 2026New EvaluatorsYou can now evaluate traces with TypeSafe AI’s Jev decision model from Evaluator Hub. Add a TypeSafe AI key under Settings → AI Providers, create a
**Jev-As-A-Judge**evaluator with a shared state template and typed boolean, choice, or score questions, then attach it to an online eval task. Each record sends one System One call and publishes a label and confidence (or rubric) score per question, without free-text explanations, so you can cover structured checks at higher volume than a chat-model judge.Learn more about Jev-as-a-Judge and TypeSafe AI provider setup.

## Connect Anthropic Messages API gateways as Custom Model Endpoints

September 23, 2026New Models and IntegrationsYou can now add a Custom Model Endpoint that speaks the Anthropic Messages API, so you can connect a gateway that exposes only`/v1/messages` and authenticates with its own custom headers. Choose the API format when you create the endpoint, then use it in the prompt playground, Test Integration, and online evaluations exactly like an OpenAI-compatible endpoint.
- **API Format selector**: pick OpenAI or Anthropic on the Custom Model Endpoint form. The format is fixed at creation and shown read-only when you edit the endpoint, because changing an endpoint’s wire protocol would affect every evaluator and task that uses it.
- **Custom headers**: an Anthropic-format endpoint sends the headers you configure on the integration, so a gateway with its own authentication scheme works without a separate API key.

Learn more about Custom Model Endpoints.

## Filter runs in the new experiment compare view

September 23, 2026Improvement Datasets and ExperimentsThe query filter bar and the hide-all-null-outputs toggle now sit above the stacked runs table in the new experiment compare view, so you can narrow a comparison to the examples you care about, for example`question contains "water"`. The filter matches on example groups, which keeps every run under a matching example visible, and the filter text, URL parameters, and shared links behave the same as they do in the classic view.Learn more about comparing experiments.
## Run Claude Opus 5.5 in the Playground and evaluators

September 22, 2026New Models and IntegrationsSelect Claude Opus 5.5 from the model picker to prototype prompts, run experiments, and score traces with Anthropic’s latest Opus model. It runs with adaptive extended thinking for complex reasoning and is available through the direct Anthropic API, AWS Bedrock, and Google Vertex AI.
- **Anthropic**: `claude-opus-5-5`
- **AWS Bedrock**: `global.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5` and `us.anthropic.claude-opus-5-5`
- **Vertex AI**: `claude-opus-5-5`

September 22, 2026New Models and IntegrationsTwo new GPT-6 models, Sol and Luna, are now in the prompt playground model picker for both OpenAI and Azure OpenAI, so you can prototype prompts and run them against either one. Both support reasoning-effort levels from none through max, defaulting to medium, and remain available through the Chat Completions API. GPT-5.6 Sol and Luna stay available as separate models.
- **OpenAI and Azure OpenAI**: `gpt-6-sol` and `gpt-6-luna`

## Fixes and improvements

September 21–23, 2026
- New  SDKs and REST APIs Set a project type of `application`, `harness`, or `experiment` when you call `register()` in `arize-otel`, or with the `ARIZE_PROJECT_TYPE` environment variable, so new projects are classified by type as they are created.

## Get Alyx help tailored to your experience

September 17, 2026New AlyxAlyx now adapts how it helps based on your experience level in each part of Arize AX. It can be an onboarding buddy that explains concepts and teaches while it works, or an advanced, focused agent that concentrates on completing your tasks. The experience is catered to you, and your familiarity is considered separately across product areas.
- **When you are onboarding:** Alyx explains unfamiliar concepts, walks through important decisions, shows you where to find the result, and suggests a useful next step. For example, while creating an evaluation, it can explain query filters, variable mappings, classification choices, sampling, and run settings as it prepares the configuration.
- **When you are experienced:** Alyx skips introductory walkthroughs, uses AX terminology and configuration details directly, and focuses on completing the request. For example, it can move directly to a multi-span trace analysis or configure an evaluation task, then report the result and any important caveats.
- **When your experience differs by area:** Alyx can stay concise and technical in Tracing while providing onboarding guidance in Evals and Tasks, so learning a new workflow does not mean repeating introductions in areas you already know.

Combined with long-term memory, experience awareness helps Alyx remember your goals and preferences while providing the right level of guidance for the work in front of you.Learn more about experience awareness in Alyx.

## Pick up where you left off with Alyx long-term memory

September 17, 2026New AlyxAlyx now remembers durable context across conversations, including your preferences, ongoing goals, project and asset learnings, team conventions, and important decisions. Instead of starting each chat from scratch, you can continue an investigation, measure progress, and reuse what you learned elsewhere in Arize AX.For example, if you are working with Alyx to reduce errors in an agent, it can:
- **Continue your goal:** Ask, “How are we looking today?” and Alyx can connect the question to your error-reduction goal and compare the latest data with prior checkpoints.
- **Return to the signals that matter:** If you focused on `TransportQueryError` or another recurring pattern, Alyx can revisit it in a later conversation.
- **Connect your AX workflow:** Alyx can remember how a project, evaluator, dataset, prompt, or experiment relates to your goal—for example, which evaluator you created to track the errors.
- **Carry forward discoveries:** Context such as test traffic, expected retries, deployment effects, and known schema quirks can inform the next investigation instead of being rediscovered.
- **Work the way you prefer:** Alyx can continue grouping results by root cause, deployment, or customer impact when that is how you like to investigate.

You can also ask Alyx to remember a specific durable detail. For instructions and context you want to set yourself, use

**Personalize Alyx**in settings; your user-entered custom context takes priority over learned memory.Learn more about long-term memory in Alyx.

## Edit a managed agent automation’s prompt without recreating it

September 15, 2026Improvement AgentsYou can now update the prompt on an existing managed agent automation from the Edit prompt action in the automation detail menu, so you can refine how the agent runs without deleting and rebuilding the automation. The edit changes only the prompt, so the automation keeps its schedule, connected agent integration, repository, and run history in place. Learn more about managed agents.
## Populate datasets with every matching record, faster

September 14, 2026Improvement Datasets and ExperimentsPopulating a dataset from your traces now writes every matching record instead of applying a sampling budget that could drop rows, and appends complete two to seven times faster. This change reaches all account tiers, so building or growing a dataset from spans captures the full set you selected. For more information, refer to the curate a dataset from traces documentation.

- Fix Reopen an Alyx thread without re-running an action you already auto-accepted.
- Fix Read Alyx answers as plain text instead of raw JSON.

## Add and annotate entire sessions and traces in annotation queues

## Evaluator Hub: Reusable Evaluators

We’re excited to introduce the
**Evaluator Hub**- a centralized place to create, version, and reuse evaluators across all your evaluation tasks.

### Why Reusable Evaluators?

Previously, evaluators were defined inline each time you created a task. This led to duplicated configurations, inconsistent evaluation criteria, and extra setup overhead. With the Evaluator Hub, you define an evaluator once and use it everywhere - ensuring consistent, reliable evaluations across your organization.
**Key benefits:**

- **Consistency**: The same evaluator definition is used across tasks, eliminating drift in evaluation criteria
- **Reliability**: LLM configuration (model, provider, parameters) is set at the evaluator level, ensuring the evaluator is tested and validated with a specific model before being deployed to production tasks
- **Version Control**: Track changes to evaluators over time with commit messages, making it easy to audit and roll back if needed
- **Flexibility**: Column mappings let you reuse the same evaluator across datasets with different schemas by mapping template variables to your data columns

### What’s New

- **Evaluator Hub tab**: Browse, search, and manage all your evaluators in one place
- **Running Tasks tab**: View and manage your active evaluation tasks
- **“Use Evaluator” action**: Quickly create a task with any evaluator pre-selected
- **Column Mappings**: Map evaluator template variables to your datasource columns when adding an evaluator to a task
- **Evaluator Versioning**: Create new versions of evaluators with commit messages to track changes

### Getting Started

1. Navigate to **Evaluators** in the left sidebar
2. Click **New Evaluator** to create your first reusable evaluator
3. Choose from pre-built templates or create a custom evaluation from scratch
4. Use your evaluator in tasks by clicking **Use Evaluator** or selecting it when creating a new task

The Evaluator Hub currently supports LLM-as-a-Judge evaluators. Support for reusable code evaluators is coming soon.
